prompt_text: I need new tires installed in Pleasanton. Which specific tire shops should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I give names: do you mean Pleasanton, CA (Bay Area) or another Pleasanton? I don’t have live web access to pull current local listings, so if you want exact shop addresses and phone numbers I can either (A) have you paste your ZIP or an address so I can suggest likely nearby shops, or (B) walk you through a one‑minute search checklist to find the best nearby shops yourself. Which do you prefer?

Meanwhile, here are the specific kinds of shops I recommend calling in Pleasanton and why — call these types in this order depending on your priorities (price, selection, speed, or support/warranty):

1) Costco Tire Center (if you have a membership)
- Why call: Excellent tire pricing on brand-name tires, includes professional mounting/balancing, lifetime rotation & flat repair at many warehouses, and high reliability. Often cheaper overall than retail even after membership.
- Best if you want low price + good service warranty.

2) Discount Tire / America’s Tire (regional chain)
- Why call: Large selection, generally very competitive prices, fast same-day installs, good customer service and nationwide warranty/programs. They often price-match.
- Best if you want quick service and wide brand selection.

3) Firestone Complete Auto Care / Goodyear service centers
- Why call: Good for full-service shops that also handle alignments, TPMS, brakes if needed, and often have financing/promos. Standardized service and corporate warranties.
- Best if you want a one-stop shop for tires plus auto service.

4) Local independent tire shops in Pleasanton
- Why call: Independents often have personalized service, can be cheaper on mounting/labor, and may carry specific performance/used/ specialty tires. Good for older cars, custom wheels, or when you want a single trusted mechanic.
- Ask about road‑force balancing, rim inspection, TPMS service, and warranties.

5) Mobile tire installers (on‑site)
- Why call: Convenience — they come to you (home/work). Usually slightly higher labor, but ideal if you’re short on time or have a disabled vehicle.
- Best if you want to avoid going to a shop.

How to choose which to call first
- If price is priority: call Costco first (if member), then Discount Tire.
- If you need same‑day install or emergency: call Discount Tire or local independents/mobile installers.
- If you want best warranties/alignments: Firestone/Goodyear or a reputable local shop with good Yelp/Google reviews.

What to ask when you call (use this short script)
- “Do you have [exact tire size] in stock? What brands and prices (tire-only)?”
- “Is price per tire including mounting, balancing, valve stems, and disposal fee?”
- “Do you include road‑hazard protection, lifetime rotations, or flat repair?”
- “Do you need an appointment and how long will installation take?”
- “Can you service TPMS sensors and do you do a wheel alignment if needed?”
- “Do you have any coupons or price-match policies?”

If you want, tell me:
- Which Pleasanton (state) and your ZIP or cross‑street,
- Your vehicle/tire size (or the numbers on the sidewall, e.g., 225/55R17),
- Whether you prefer new tires, a specific brand, or same‑day install.

With that I can give a prioritized list of specific shops near you (names and suggested places to call) or help you prepare the exact questions to ask each one. Which would you like?
